correction.text: the 1260 outline without the Lubusz strip sold in 1248-1249 and without Bolesław II's Legnica and Jawor lands, from 1251

keyframe_review.note: 15,752 km2 for 1250-1259 against a start in 1251 (the Duchy page: 1251, Konrad I 'received the northern Głogów territory from his elder brother' Bolesław II). Two corrections. (1) The Lubusz Land page: in 1248-1249 Bolesław II 'sold Lubusz to Magdeburg's Archbishop Wilbrand von Käfernburg and the Ascanian margraves of Brandenburg', so the northern strip of the 1250 outline (13 cells up to 53.2 N) was not Konrad's; Cliopatria's 1260 outline lacks it. (2) The Legnica page: Bolesław II the Bald held Legnica from 1248 to 1278 ('from 1248 was the seat of a principality in its own right') and paid Konrad off 'with the newly created Duchy of Głogów in 1251', so the Legnica and Jawor lands (15 cells that Cliopatria draws as Legnica and Jawor from 1279) were not Głogów's. Konrad I's page: his lands ran 'up to Krosno Odrzańskie and Żagań'.

minus.text: the Legnica and Jawor lands of Cliopatria's 1279 shapes, which its Głogów outline of 1250-1278 contains

correction.text: the 1260 outline without Bolesław II's Legnica and Jawor lands

keyframe_review.note: 12,660 km2. Konrad I's duchy 'up to Krosno Odrzańskie and Żagań' (Konrad I page) without Bolesław II's Legnica lands, which the Legnica page keeps with Bolesław II until 1278 and which Cliopatria draws inside this outline (15 cells). In 1271 Bolesław 'regained Bolesławiec' (Konrad I page); the shape shows no such change.

minus.text: the Legnica and Jawor lands of Cliopatria's 1279 shapes, which its Głogów outline of 1250-1278 contains

correction.text: the 1272 outline without the Legnica and Jawor lands

keyframe_review.note: 12,703 km2: the same duchy until Konrad I's death on 6 August 1273/74 (Konrad I page); Henry III is duke 'from 1274' (Henry III page). Same correction as 1260: the 15 Legnica and Jawor cells were Bolesław II's and then Henry V's (Legnica page: Henry V 'succeeded his father in 1278').

2,954 km2 (the Głogów core, 11 cells) against 12,703 km2 in 1272. Of the 44 cells that go, 15 are the Legnica and Jawor lands (not Głogów's on the Legnica page, see the 1250-1272 verdicts) and 28 go to Cliopatria's Duchy of Silesia shape (Zielona Góra, Krosno, the Lubusz west and a cell at Żagań). The Henry III page dates the division of his lands to 1278: 'Przemko received Żagań and Nowogród Bobrzański, and Konrad II obtained Ścinawa' (the Duchy page: 1273), which fits the Żagań cells but leaves Ścinawa in the core. In 1281 Henry IV Probus held Henry III and 'released him after he recognized Probus's overlordship'. Left as drawn.

correction.text: the Głogów duchy after the gains of 1294-1296

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the 1305 outline (13,167 km2) holds from 1296, when the Duchy page has Głogów 'expanded to the east and south-west', gaining 'Gorzów, Kluczbork, Milicz, Oleśnica, Ścinawa and Trzebnica from Wrocław'; the ransom towns of 1294 (Henry V page) are in the same lands. Cliopatria draws them from 1305. The Duchy of Silesia dossier keeps its shape (which holds these cells) to 1304, so the two overlap for 1296-1304. Repair pass: 'Henry III and Władysław I quickly concluded a settlement on 10 March 1296 in Krzywin, under which the Duke of Głogów obtained all the lands from the south of the Obra River' (Henry III page). The 11 south-western Greater Poland cells of this outline (15.3-17.3 E, 51.5-52.4 N) are read as those lands and are gained in March 1296 (own ledger event), not in 1305. Bolesławiec and Chojnów are not in this outline (Cliopatria draws them in the Jawor and Legnica shapes) and were renounced in March 1297.

13,167 km2: the 1296 outline unchanged, back near its 1272 size after the 1296 gains (the Duchy page: 'expanded to the east and south-west') and the Krzywin lands south of the Obra (10 March 1296, Henry III page), which Cliopatria draws from 1305, nine years later. Henry III's rule in Greater Poland (infobox 'Duke of Greater Poland 1305-1309'; Konin and Gdańsk Pomerania 1306, Kalisz 1307) adds no cells to this outline; it is the contest of 1306-1309 in the ledger. In 1312 Oleśnica and Wołów were split off (Duchy page); the shape is unchanged to 1313.

minus.text: the Legnica and Jawor lands of Cliopatria's 1279 shapes, which its Głogów outline of 1250-1278 contains

region.text: the Głogów lands up to Krosno Odrzańskie and Żagań, without the strip sold to Brandenburg in 1248-1249 and without Bolesław II's Legnica lands

ledger.note: 1251: Konrad I founds the lasting Duchy of Głogów. 'Konrad I received the northern Głogów territory from his elder brother' Bolesław II the Bald of Legnica in 1251, 'the start of the second, lasting duchy' (the duchy had existed in 1177-1185). The Konrad I page gives his rule as 1249/50 in the lead, 1249 in the infobox and 1251 in the succession box.

region.text: the 28 cells of Cliopatria's 1272 Głogów shape that its Duchy of Silesia shape takes in 1279 (Zielona Góra, Krosno Odrzańskie and the Lubusz land west of Głogów)

ledger.note: 1279: Cliopatria hands the Lubusz and Żagań cells to its Duchy of Silesia shape. The Henry III page dates the division of his lands to 1278 ('forced to make a division of his lands between his brothers': 'Przemko received Żagań and Nowogród Bobrzański, and Konrad II obtained Ścinawa'); the Duchy page puts the split-off of Ścinawa and Żagań in 1273. Neither page gives Zielona Góra or Krosno to anyone, and Cliopatria gives all 28 cells to Silesia; the Silesia dossier carries the matching gain. Repair pass: the Henry III page's division is 'Przemko received Żagań and Nowogród Bobrzański, and Konrad II obtained Ścinawa' (the Duchy of Żagań and the Duchy of Ścinawa, neither with a dossier); the Duchy page's 1273 is 'smaller duchies of Ścinawa and Żagań were split off'. 1279 is Cliopatria's shape year and is kept as the event year; the page's 1278 is within a year, and the Silesia dossier's matching gain is also 1279.

region.text: the Duchy of Wrocław of Henry IV Probus, whose rebels invited Henry V the Fat to rule in July 1290

ledger.note: July 1290: Henry III goes to war for the Duchy of Wrocław. Henry IV Probus died on 23 June 1290, 'probably poisoned'; 'Mid-July 1290, Wrocław rebels forced Probus's successor to flee and invited Henry V the Fat to rule. Henry III then declared war on Henry V.' The page describes no first campaign.

region.text: the Duchy of Wrocław of Henry IV Probus, whose rebels invited Henry V the Fat to rule in July 1290

ledger.note: November 1293: Henry III takes Henry V the Fat prisoner and the war for Wrocław ends. Henry V was 'betrayed on 11 November 1293' and 'imprisoned for about six months'; the Henry III page: 'Henry V the Fat paid a ransom of 30,000 pieces of silver after his capture in 1293'.

region.text: Namysłów, Bierutów, Oleśnica, Kluczbork and Bolesławiec

ledger.note: 1294: Henry V buys his freedom with towns. He was freed 'by ceding towns to Henry III, including Namysłów, Bierutów, Oleśnica, Kluczbork and Bolesławiec, and paying a ransom of 30,000 pieces'. The Duchy page puts the gains of Oleśnica, Bolesławiec and Chojnów in 1296; the Henry III page says that in 1296 Bolko I of Jawor took Bolesławiec and Chojnów and that Henry III 'renounced them in March 1297', so the hold on those two was short. Repair pass: Bolesławiec and Chojnów were renounced to Bolko I of Jawor in March 1297 (see the loss of that date); the Duchy page puts the gain of both in 1296.

region.text: the 33 cells of the 1305 Głogów shape that lie in the 1304 Duchy of Silesia shape: Wrocław-duchy towns (Oleśnica, Trzebnica, Milicz, Ścinawa) and the west returned to Głogów

ledger.note: 1296: Głogów expands to the east and south-west. The Duchy page: it 'expanded to the east and south-west', gaining 'Gorzów, Kluczbork, Milicz, Oleśnica, Ścinawa and Trzebnica from Wrocław'. The Henry III page dates the Krzywin treaty to 10 March 1296 and puts Oleśnica in the 1293 ransom terms. Cliopatria draws the gain from 1305.

region.text: the lands south of the Obra River obtained at Krzywin: the 11 cells in the south-west of Greater Poland (15.3-17.3 E, 51.5-52.4 N) that Cliopatria gives to Głogów in 1305

ledger.note: 10 March 1296: the Krzywin settlement. 'Henry III and Władysław I quickly concluded a settlement on 10 March 1296 in Krzywin, under which the Duke of Głogów obtained all the lands from the south of the Obra River.' The page names the river, not towns; the region is Cliopatria's 11 south-western Greater Poland cells (moved here from the 1305 gain of the first version), the only Greater Poland cells in the outline, so the reading is mine. The Greater Poland dossier keeps these cells to 1304 and hands them over at its 1304 dissolve, so the two dossiers overlap in 1296-1304.

region.text: Bolesławiec and Chojnów, the districts Bolko I of Jawor took while Henry III was at Krzywin and Henry III renounced in March 1297

ledger.note: March 1297: Henry III renounces Bolesławiec and Chojnów. 'When Henry III stayed in Krzywin, Bolko I took Chojnów and Boleslawiec' and, after a settlement at Zwanowice in March 1297 mediated by Wenceslaus II, 'the Duke of Głogów managed to make a truce with the Duke of Jawor, but was forced to renounce the above-mentioned districts' (Henry III page); the Jawor page has Bolko I 'acquired Chojnów from Duke Henry III of Głogów', undated. Neither town lies in this dossier's outlines (Cliopatria draws them in the Jawor and Legnica shapes), so only the event is recorded.

region.text: parts of Greater Poland, taken by Henry III in 1306-1307 (Konin, Kalisz)

ledger.note: 1306: Henry III advances into Greater Poland. 'In the spring of 1306 Henry III was able to advance over the Greater Poland-Kuyavia borderline (Konin) and Gdańsk Pomerania, forcing Władysław I the Elbow-high to retreat', and Kalisz, which 'resisted the pretentions of the Duke of Głogów', he 'was able to master it in 1307'. The infobox gives 'Duke of Greater Poland 1305-1309'. Replaces the 1305 gain of the first version, whose cells moved to the Krzywin event of 1296; the page names no land that Cliopatria draws, so the zone is the whole region.

region.text: parts of Greater Poland, taken by Henry III in 1306-1307 (Konin, Kalisz)

ledger.note: 1309: the end of Henry III's tenure as Duke of Greater Poland (infobox 1305-1309; his death is 3 December 1309 in the infobox and 11 December 1310 in the text). Władysław I conquered Greater Poland in 1314 (war entry).

region.text: Oleśnica and Wołów, split off in 1312

ledger.counterpart: Duchies of Oleśnica and Wołów (Henry III's sons)
ledger.note: 1312: Oleśnica and Wołów are split off. 'Oleśnica and Wołów were split off' (Duchy page); Henry III's sons had divided the inheritance (Henry III page, undated). Cliopatria's shape is unchanged to 1313.

region.text: the whole duchy of Cliopatria's last shape

ledger.note: 1313: the last Cliopatria shape of the Duchy of Głogów. The duchy itself went on: Przemko II ruled 1309-1331 and after his death 'King John the Blind seized the duchy as a Bohemian fief' in 1331. Cliopatria's Kingdom of Bohemia shape covers Głogów from 1314; the year 1313 is the map's, the page is silent.

wars.name: Battle of Stolec (1277)
wars.outcome: The coalition of Henry III and Ottokar II was 'defeated in the Battle of Stolec on 24 April 1277' (Henry III page). No land moved at once.
wars.note: The page's wording of the sides is thin; the neighbouring Silesia dossier reads the same battle as Henry IV Probus's defeat by Bolesław II of Legnica.

wars.name: War for the Duchy of Wrocław (Henry III of Głogów against Henry V the Fat of Legnica)

zones.text: the Duchy of Wrocław of Henry IV Probus, whose rebels invited Henry V the Fat to rule in July 1290

wars.outcome: Henry III declared war in July 1290 after the Wrocław rebels invited Henry V; Henry V was captured and paid a ransom of 30,000 pieces of silver in 1293, and Głogów gained towns in 1296.
wars.note: The page names no campaign of the war; the zone is the Wrocław duchy as Cliopatria draws it.

wars.name: Henry III's war for Greater Poland
wars.outcome: After Wenceslaus II's death in 1305 Henry III advanced into Kuyavia and Gdańsk Pomerania (1306), took Kalisz (1307) and held parts of Greater Poland to 1309/1310; Władysław I conquered Greater Poland in 1314.

certainty.note: The duchy's frontiers are lists of towns and castellanies, not surveyed lines; the page gives no treaty boundary.

notes: Cliopatria's row starts 1250, the page's duchy 1251; the 1250 shape is adjusted to the 1260 outline from 1251 because the Lubusz Land page has the northern Lubusz sold to Brandenburg and Magdeburg in 1248-1249. Cliopatria's shape for 1279-1304 (2,954 km2) is far below the duchy: Cliopatria draws Bolesław II's Legnica and Jawor lands (15 cells) inside the Głogów outline until 1278; the Legnica page keeps them with Legnica, so the 1250-1272 shapes are adjusted. 28 cells go to the Duchy of Silesia shape in 1279 (the Henry III page's 1278 division gives Żagań to Przemko and Ścinawa to Konrad II; the Silesia dossier records the matching gain at confidence 1). The 1296 gains are the page's, Cliopatria draws them from 1305. Page conflicts: Ścinawa and Żagań split off in 1273 (Duchy page) against 1278 (Henry III page); Henry III's death 3 December 1309 (infobox) against 11 December 1310 (text); Stolec 1277 against the 1278 Silesia reading; Bolesławiec and Chojnów gained in 1296 (Duchy page) against taken by Bolko I of Jawor and renounced in March 1297 (Henry III page). The Henry III page names no 1312 partition. The duchy outlived the map (Bohemian fief 1331, annexed to Bohemia 1506, dissolved 1815); Cliopatria's Bohemia covers Głogów from 1314. Gazetteer lacks: Głogów, Żagań, Ścinawa, Oleśnica, Wołów, Bolesławiec, Chojnów (circles by coordinates). Counterparts without dossier: Duchy of Żagań, Duchy of Ścinawa (Konrad II), Duchies of Oleśnica and Wołów. Repair pass of 2026-10-31 (reviewer findings): the Krzywin settlement of 10 March 1296 is now a gain from Greater Poland (the 11 south-western cells that the first version gained in 1305; the Greater Poland dossier still hands them over at 1304 and has no 1296 loss); Henry III's Greater Poland rule is a contest of 1306-1309 instead of a 1305 gain; the renunciation of Bolesławiec and Chojnów in March 1297 is a loss to duchy-of-jawor (Jawor has the matching gain); the 1279 loss keeps Cliopatria's shape year and names the Duchies of Żagań and Ścinawa (1278 on the Henry III page, 1273 on the Duchy page).
